title: Add M6 Layer 2 painted constraints: 6 brush types, 3-layer validation, sim integration
description:
## M6 — Layer 2 Painted Constraints

Per .design/realistic-planet-generator.md REQ-8 + REQ-9, AC-8 + AC-9, and design.md §6.2 + §6.3 + §7.5. Builds on M0-M5 (now main HEAD `ce84ae6`).

### In scope

1. **Brush UI infrastructure (`src/components/ConstraintBrush/`)**:
   - `BrushSelector.tsx`: toolbar with 6 brush types, brush radius slider.
   - `BrushCursor.tsx`: visual brush cursor on globe (raycast from camera through cursor to sphere intersection, identify cells under brush radius).
   - `CurveDrawer.tsx`: for boundary/coastline brushes — click to place control points, double-click to finish, curve auto-snaps to existing painted plates.
   - Click-drag paints; right-click erases painted constraints; esc exits constraint mode.

2. **Six brush types (`src/constraints/brushes/`)**:
   - **`plate.ts`** — paint a region as belonging to a specific plate. Optionally specify continental/oceanic, Euler pole, rotation rate. Adjacent unpainted area gets plates assigned to satisfy global constraints.
   - **`boundary.ts`** — draw a curve on the sphere; tag as convergent/divergent/transform; optionally specify rate. Sim places boundary geometry along the curve.
   - **`feature.ts`** — feature pins: mountain range (along curve = convergent boundary), volcanic arc (oceanic-under-continental subduction with trench offshore), rift (continental divergent boundary), hotspot (fixed mantle-frame point with optional activation history), ancient orogen (eroded mountain range with specified age).
   - **`climate.ts`** — paint a cell or region with intended biome. Sim treats as soft constraint; validates that painted biome is consistent with computed (T, P); if inconsistent, reports issue with fix suggestion.
   - **`coastline.ts`** — trace a coastline. Sim treats as hard constraint on continental edge.
   - **`settlement.ts`** — Layer 2.5; runs after physical sim. Capital/city/town/village markers, trade route corridors. Used downstream of biomes; doesn't affect physical sim.

3. **Constraint data model (`src/constraints/types.ts`)**:
   - Discriminated union over the 6 brush types.
   - Cell-keyed sparse storage for plate/climate constraints.
   - Curve-based storage for boundary/coastline (control points + smoothed curve cells).
   - Point-based for hotspots and settlement pins.

4. **Three-layer validation (`src/constraints/validate.ts`, `src/constraints/suggest.ts`)**:
   - **Hard validation at input time** (`validate.ts`):
     - Painted plate boundaries form closed loops.
     - Total convergence equals total divergence (within tolerance).
     - Specified Euler poles produce the painted boundary motions.
     - Hotspot tracks consistent with plate motion direction.
     - Coastlines don't cross plate boundaries except at convergent margins.
     - Surfaces failures with red overlay (errors) / yellow overlay (warnings) + panel listing each issue with location.
   - **Soft constraints with relaxation during sim**: fold into objective function the sim minimizes during equilibration. Allow user to mark constraints "preferred" (relaxable) or "required" (hard).
   - **Resolution suggestions** (`suggest.ts`): when validation fails, propose specific fixes ("Adjust Euler pole to X" / "Change track direction" / "Mark hotspot as recently activated").

5. **Continuous validation during paint**: debounced to ~200ms. Validation runs as the user paints, error overlays update live.

6. **Sim integration**:
   - Worker accepts `setConstraints(constraints: Constraint[]): Promise<ValidationIssue[]>` per design.md §7.4.
   - Tectonics stage (M1) reads painted plate IDs, boundaries, hotspots and respects them as boundary conditions during init.
   - Erosion/hydrology stages don't need constraint awareness — they operate on the elevation field that tectonics produces.
   - Climate pins as soft constraints folded into the equilibration objective.
   - Coastline pins as hard constraints on land/ocean classification.

7. **Visual overlay (`src/components/ConstraintOverlays.tsx`)**: painted constraints render as semi-transparent layers over the globe — colored by brush type, with hard/soft distinction (solid/dashed border).

8. **Tests**:
   - Each brush type's constraint data round-trips through Zustand + IDB.
   - Hard validation rejects intentionally inconsistent constraint sets (5 fixtures: hotspot misaligned, coastline crosses transform, climate inconsistent, boundary loop incomplete, Euler pole mismatch).
   - Soft constraint relaxation reduces objective monotonically across iterations (synthetic test).
   - Resolution suggestions provide ≥1 fix for each failure mode.
   - Brush operations (click-drag, right-click erase, esc cancel, curve double-click) work in jsdom test.

### Out of scope (do not start)
- M7 regional refinement.
- M8/M10 civilization layer.
- VTT exports (Foundry/Roll20 still deferred).

### Acceptance criteria for M6 (from AC-8 + AC-9)
- [ ] All 6 brush types paint constraint data persistable across sessions; brush radius, click-drag, right-click erase, esc-cancel functional.
- [ ] A test fixture of inconsistent constraints produces red overlay + listed issue + ≥1 fix per case.
- [ ] Soft-constraint relaxation reduces objective monotonically across iterations.
- [ ] Hard validation runs continuously during paint, debounced to ~200ms (microbenchmark).
- [ ] M0-M5 test suites still pass after M6 changes (regression).
- [ ] `npm test` + `tsc --noEmit` both pass.
- [ ] No stubs / TODOs.

### Lesson from prior milestones
**Commit each major group as you finish.** M5 nailed this with 6 commits. M6 has natural commit groups: brush types, constraint data model, validation, suggestions, sim integration, UI overlay, tests. Aim for 6-8 commits.

### References
- .design/realistic-planet-generator.md REQ-8 / REQ-9 / AC-8 / AC-9, plus REQ-2 (constraints feed into causality)
- design.md §6.2 (Layer 2), §6.3 (validation), §7.5 (constraint UX), §3 (worker boundary contract)
- M5 main HEAD `ce84ae6` provides Layer 1 + UI + persistence to build on
